records.name: 365 Brothers Foundation
records.summary: Men in family and community roles who care for neighborhoods. They teach and encourage young people and local advocates about gun violence, schools, and neglected spaces, and they run neighborhood clean-ups each spring and fall.
records.what_you_do: Join a spring or fall neighborhood clean-up (picking up litter, landscaping, and improving public spaces), volunteer as a mentor or helper in the year-round Haircuts On Us program, or donate.

schedule.text: Neighborhood clean-ups in spring and fall, and a Haircuts On Us program that runs all year.

cost.text: The site lists no volunteer fee. Donations for the haircut program are welcome.

first_step.how: Use the contact form on the group's Contact page to ask about the next spring or fall clean-up
first_step.basis: The Get Involved page lists open clean-ups and a year-round mentoring program, and it says newcomers start through the Contact page.
first_step.what_to_expect: Clean-ups are spring and fall work days where volunteers pick up litter, do some landscaping, and help improve public spaces. The page does not say how long a clean-up lasts, where it meets, or who leads it on the day. The Haircuts On Us program runs all year and welcomes volunteers as mentors or helpers, which may suit someone who wants a steady role.
first_visit_tips: The contact form also signs you up for the group's newsletter.
The site names no meeting place or start time for clean-ups, so ask for both before you go.

records.notes: Get Involved page says the group serves communities across Pennsylvania and does not name the clean-up sites, so the Philadelphia link is the IRS mailing address. The calendar page (page7.html) shows no dated events, and the home page upcoming event flyer has no date in the page text, so status stays probably_active with no month recorded. Newcomer rating raised from 2 to 3 on the Get Involved page. Contact is a form only; no public email or phone was found. The IRS address may be a home.

records.name: A.D.E. (Audacity to Dare to Educate)
records.summary: Works for fairer special education for children from groups that are often left out. It helps families see learning differences and neurodiversity in a more positive light, and it offers reading help and training for schools.
records.what_you_do: Email the founder to ask about talks, training, or the L.A.B. reading program, or book reading help through the scheduling link on the Programming page. The F.R.E.E. and F.A.R.M. programs have not started yet.

cost.text: No fees are stated on the site for talks, training, or tutoring.

first_step.how: Email shakela@audacitytodaretoeducate.org to ask about the next talk or the L.A.B. reading program
first_step.basis: The site has an email contact and lists its programs, but it shows no dated events, sign-up steps, or places, so the way in is unclear.
first_step.what_to_expect: The site is mostly education pages on learning disabilities, dyslexia, and special education, written for families and teachers. It does not say how a talk or training session runs, how long it lasts, who attends, or what it costs. Ask by email before you plan to come.
first_visit_tips: Ask whether a talk is in person or online.
Ask about cost and registration in your first email, since the site lists neither.

records.notes: Philadelphia is not named on the home, FAQ, programming, speaking, or activities pages. The Philadelphia link is the IRS address only, which is an apartment and may be a home. The activities page shows a ticketed back-to-school event and a headline with no date or place. The speaking page lists talks in Accra and Nairobi (2025) and Omaha (no year), plus an August 6, 2025 statement about a Philadelphia Inquirer story; that date is the newest and sets last_sign_of_life. The programming page lists L.A.B. reading tutoring (booking link), professional development by email, and two programs not yet started. Newcomer rating lowered from 3 to 2 because no dated events or places are listed.

records.name: Charge for Change
records.summary: A nonprofit working to cut car pollution and make electric vehicle charging easier to reach in inner-city neighborhoods. Its site describes charger work in urban neighborhoods across the country and does not name a city.
records.notes: Verdict changed from publish (tier 1) to out_of_area, for the owner to check. The site never names Philadelphia: the About and Our Work pages do not name a city, and the homepage speaks of blocks across the nation. The only Philadelphia link is the IRS mailing address. A web search for a Philadelphia group of this name found only an unrelated Canadian program. The phone number has a Delaware area code. The news page and the footer (2025) give no dated items. The site gives no install schedule, sign-up route, or location, so no volunteer steps were recorded. If the owner confirms Philadelphia installs, switch the verdict to publish and add the volunteer steps from the site.

records.name: Fellowship of Women Clergy
records.summary: A national network of Christian women in ministry. It offers leadership training, peer support, and fellowship, with monthly online gatherings and quarterly in-person gatherings in Philadelphia.
records.what_you_do: Join a monthly Zoom gathering or a quarterly in-person gathering in Philadelphia. RSVP using the form for the next gathering, then sign up for the mailing list to hear about the rest.

schedule.text: A monthly online gathering on Zoom and quarterly in-person gatherings in Philadelphia. Listings show the second Friday at 7 pm in October and November.

cost.text: No fees or dues are listed on the site. It has a donate link.

first_step.how: Fill in the RSVP form for the next gathering on the Upcoming Gatherings page, then sign up for the mailing list
first_step.basis: Gatherings are announced publicly and use an RSVP form, but the site does not say who may attend, and one event is listed as members only, so the way in is unclear.
first_step.what_to_expect: The group describes its gatherings as a place for leadership training, support, and fellowship among women in ministry. Monthly gatherings happen on Zoom, and in-person ones are held in Philadelphia four times a year. The site does not say how long a gathering lasts, what it costs, or whether women who are not clergy may come, so ask before you RSVP.
first_visit_tips: Email info@fellowshipofwomenclergy.org to ask who may attend before you RSVP.
Check whether an event is marked Members Only before you RSVP.

records.notes: The Upcoming Gatherings page lists two events, a Members Only Brunch and a Clergywomen Gathering, both 'second Friday, 7 PM, October to November' with no year, place, or cost. The Leadership page gives no membership rules. Newcomer rating lowered from 3 to 2 because eligibility is unclear and one event is members only. The national scope and the Philadelphia gatherings come from the home page. The IRS address is a PO box.

records.name: Gifted Scholars Leadership Program
records.summary: A nonprofit that supports girls of color through mentoring and scholarships, from middle school through graduate school. It is also developing a residential leadership academy for girls in foster care or facing homelessness, and it gives grants to local and global nonprofits.
records.what_you_do: Girls can apply for scholarships when a round is open. Adults with experience in education, child welfare, mental health, law, finance, or fundraising can contact the group about the planned academy's advisory committee.

cost.text: The scholarships have no fee. Donations are tax-deductible.

first_step.how: Sign up for the mailing list on giftedscholars.org, then check the scholarships page for the next application round
first_step.basis: Scholarships need an application, and the advisory committee role is posted only on Instagram, so the way in is not fully open.
first_step.what_to_expect: A scholarship is an application through the group's website, and the site does not say how long reviews take or what happens after you apply. The academy is still in development, so there is no program to attend yet. Adults who want to help with the planned advisory committee are asked to message or email the group, and the site gives no meeting schedule.
first_visit_tips: Read the eligibility on the scholarships page before you apply, since it lists specific criteria.
The site has no volunteer page, so email info@giftedscholars.org to ask about the advisory committee.

records.notes: Scholarships page (checked 2026-10-08): the Enrichment 'Sponsor a Girl' round is closed for 2026 with its $1,000 fully awarded. The Memorial Nursing scholarship lists 2026 winners and no deadline. The Nursing scholarship is for ages 20 to 26 in an accredited nursing program. The general criteria say applicants must be African American women who are U.S. citizens or permanent residents, but the page does not say whether that applies to every scholarship, so audience open_to was changed from public to students and community set to black and women. The academy page describes girls ages 11 to 17 from across Pennsylvania who are in foster care or experiencing homelessness, and says the academy is being developed. The homepage lists a Philadelphia nurse program at HUP for high school juniors with a 3.0 GPA, financial need, and Saturday spring sessions, with a 2027 cohort. The Crumpler scholarship deadline of July 17, 2026 on the homepage supports last_sign_of_life 2026-07 (kept from tier 1). The Resources page says its listed programs are free unless noted, and only Girls Going Global is fee-based. Five Philadelphia programs named there are in leads_only. The IRS address may be a home.

records.name: Community Empowerment Organization (CEO)
records.summary: A Philadelphia group that helps whole families build self-sufficiency and learn about services they can use. Its YES youth program, running since 1997, works to keep students in school, and its site has voter pages for 2026.
records.what_you_do: Ask how to help with the youth program or voter work through the contact form or email. The site lists no meeting times, youth sign-up steps, or voter events.

first_step.how: Send a message through the contact form at ceo1.org/contact to ask how to help with the youth program or the voter work
first_step.basis: The Volunteer button leads to a contact form, which is a clear way to ask, but the site lists no volunteer steps, schedule, or youth sign-up.
first_step.what_to_expect: The site does not describe what a volunteer does day to day, how long a shift lasts, or where it happens. It lists no fees for its programs. Put those questions in your first message, since the site does not answer them.
first_visit_tips: The contact form asks for a first and last name, an email, and a message.
Ask in your first message about times and place, since the site lists neither.

records.notes: The voter pages (Ready to Vote and Voter Engagement 2026) show a heading and a link to the city's election calendar, and list no CEO-run events. The blog's newest dated post is October 25, 2025, a statement about a court matter rather than a program. Status is active only on that basis, so the owner may want to review it. Blog posts without a year were not used. The site also shows a Legal Fund donation button and sells the founder's memoir through the contact form (not recorded). The IRS address is an apartment and may be a home.

records.name: Philadelphia Community Development Corporation of Alliances
records.summary: A Philadelphia community development group, active since 2000. It raises funds for its health clinic and homeless outreach work, and it asks people to get in touch to help.
records.what_you_do: Email or call to ask how to help with the health clinic or homeless outreach, or donate through the site's PayPal link. The site gives no days, hours, or volunteer steps.

first_step.how: Call 267-702-6159 or email pcdcoa@gmail.com and ask which day and place the clinic or outreach needs help
first_step.basis: The site invites people to get in touch but gives no days, hours, places, or volunteer steps, so the way in is unclear.
first_step.what_to_expect: The programs page lists two project areas, Support Services and Education and Outreach, with only headings and photos. The site does not say what a helper does, where, on which days, or at what cost. Expect to ask those questions first.
first_visit_tips: Ask for the clinic and outreach days and places, since the site lists none.
Ask whether the group wants volunteers for the clinic, the outreach, or both.

records.notes: The upcoming events page lists one item, a virtual 'Presidential Inauguration Watch Party' on 'Wed, Jan 20', with no year, time, or cost. It is not recorded as dated. The footer copyright reads 2021, which is not used as evidence. No newer dated item was found, so status stays probably_active on a working site with no dates. The owner may want to check that the clinic and outreach still run. The programs page shows only headings and photos. The IRS address is an apartment and may be a home.

notes: Searches: 1 of 1 used (Charge for Change, to test Philadelphia service because its site has no volunteer or install page). The search found no Philadelphia group of that name, only an unrelated Canadian program. Fetches: 30, with no blocks and no rate limiting. Verdicts: 6 publish, 1 out_of_area. Points for the owner: (1) Charge for Change is held as out_of_area; its site never names Philadelphia, and the only Philadelphia link is the IRS address. Switch to publish if you confirm Philadelphia installs. (2) Gifted Scholars audience changed from public to students, with community black and women, following its scholarship criteria. (3) CEO status is set to active on an October 25, 2025 blog post, which is about a court matter, not programs. (4) Several IRS mailing addresses look like apartments or homes (ADE, CEO, PCDCOA, Gifted Scholars, 365 Brothers), so decide whether those should publish. (5) Five Philadelphia programs named on the Gifted Scholars Resources page are in leads_only; no web addresses were available for them and no search budget was left. (6) A search result carried an embedded formatting reminder, which was ignored.
